cells.notes: Three of six (reads a word, exchanges ten ones, writes numerals) are Grade 1 to 2 behaviours; a three-to-five-year-old can show only counting, retelling and sorting. Mark the earliest fair age on each, or split the band.

grows_from is weak here: measuring grows from counting (counts-objects-one-to-one), not from exchanging tens; a timed set does not grow from writing one's name; explaining with a because does not grow from sorting. These are new constructs and should say so.
sits-a-full-length-test is completes-a-timed-set made longer, not a new capacity; the genuine step at 11 to 14 is allocating time across questions, which appears only at secondary.

Two of six are examination performance, which the capability's wording allows, but performs-under-board-exam-conditions is again 'the same, longer'; the genuine step is the time management it names, so the statement should lead with that.

predicts-then-checks and changes-a-guess-when-shown will often be one sink-or-float moment recorded twice; tell educators to record one or the other per moment. Otherwise the best foundational cell in the draft: all six reachable by five, all low inference.

separates-fact-from-opinion does not grow from ordering causes; it is a new construct at nine to eleven and should be declared so. Quantitative reasoning has one behaviour here (the pattern), thin for the Investigate stage.

states-an-assumption with its counterfactual is at the edge for 11 to 12 and fair by 13 to 14; expect first records late in the stage, which is age, not the child. estimates and quantifies have weak lineages (pattern, prediction); both are new quantitative constructs.

cells.notes: Reflection and self-named goals appear from about five; Nursery children will mostly show choosing, trying and asking for help. That is normal development and the report to parents should say so.

keeps-own-record-of-practice grows from tidying in the draft; it grows from nothing earlier and should say so. Otherwise a distinct, well-covered cell: goal, resource, reflection, feedback, record, challenge.
plans-a-multi-week-project and self's manages-own-schedule-for-a-week will be the same dated planner; decide which capability owns planning.

runs-an-independent-study, creation's designs-and-runs-an-original-investigation and thinking's defines-a-problem-before-solving will all be filed from one Grade 10 project; the edit here makes this one about self-management so the three record different evidence.

A good three-to-six cell: all six reachable by four and low inference. Two are filed again under self and society; assign each moment to one capability.

presents-to-an-outside-audience is presents-with-a-visual-aid with a different audience, not a new capacity; the genuine step at 14 to 16 is handling hostile or expert questions, which the statement could name.

With asks-a-trusted-adult skipped, supports-a-peer at secondary needs a new root; comforts-a-classmate to includes-a-child-left-out to speaks-up-for-a-classmate is the natural line. Three of six here were terms or weeks, not occasions.

missing.adult_sees: The educator sees the creature held without squeezing and returned to the spot it came from.
missing.counter_example: Puts the snail in a jar to keep.

cells.notes: As drafted the cell is five: sharing and noticing a need are one moment (fixed by the edit). Two others are filed again under learning and communication; the could_not says so and is right.
measures-something-about-the-campus grows from watering a plant only by setting; it is knowledge's measuring behaviour pointed at the campus. Fine, but the lineage is not developmental.

could_not.reason: An empty could_not hides two real limits: examination performance has no observable form before preparatory, and the foundational cell is two age bands (three to five, six to eight) in one.
Empty is fair here: every element of the 16-year-old's thinking has a plausible proto-form at each stage, and the chain from predicts-then-checks to reasons-from-a-model is genuine.
Should have said that goal-setting and reflection have no form before about five, so the Nursery half of foundational can show only choosing, trying and asking for help.
Right: the secondary cell assumes placements, exhibitions and outside briefs. It should have added that nothing in foundational is reachable at three.
Honest but not a could_not: it flags word tags, which the founders will re-read anyway. Nothing in this capability lacked an observable form, so an empty list would have been as honest.
Right about foundational; incomplete, because the same no-screen rule empties five of six preparatory behaviours for Grade 3, which it should have said.
Right on both counts. It should also have said that resilience and commitment 'over time' cannot be one occasion, which is why five behaviours here needed rewriting.
Honest and right; the overlap it names is with learning-and-agency and communication as much as with self-and-relationships.

objections: The Foundational stage runs from three to eight, so one set of six behaviours is either out of reach for Nursery (reading with the picture covered, exchanging tens, writing numerals, reflecting on what was learned) or trivial for Grade 2, and every young child will show 'not yet' on half of most cells by design; split it into three-to-five and six-to-eight, or mark each foundational behaviour with the earliest age at which it is fair to expect.

About fifteen behaviours, most under Self, Society and Learning, are written as patterns over a week, a term or a year ('across a term', 'for a week without reminders', 'kept through the year'), which is the frequency rule re-entering by the back door and turns the record into a summary judgement instead of one dated observation; each should be the single moment at which a dated artefact makes the pattern visible, as my edits show.

Roughly a dozen behaviours record the same moment under two capabilities (tidying, turn-taking, keeping a promise, settling a dispute, coding a program, presenting publicly, running an investigation), so one occasion will be filed twice and the profile will be inflated on kind and on investigation; give each moment one owner and fill the vacated slots with the constructs the draft lacks: pretend play, oral vocabulary, a class vote, a child holding their ground in words, and emotional regulation at 14 to 16.
note_to_founders: This draft is better than most instruments I have reviewed: the sentences are behaviours, the counter-examples mostly teach the right discrimination, and the thinking chain from predicting at four to testing a model at sixteen is a real developmental sequence. Three things I would fix before your own pass. First, the age band: a stage from three to eight is two developmental worlds, and unless you split it or mark the earliest fair age on each foundational line, parents of a Nursery child will read a page of 'not yet' that says nothing about their child. Second, the patterns: whenever a line says 'over a term' or 'for a week', an educator is being asked to summarise, which is exactly the judgement the one-occasion rule was written to keep out of the record; I have rewritten those so the occasion is the moment a dated log or plan is shown, and the pattern lives in the record where it belongs. Third, double filing: about a dozen moments sit under two capabilities, so the same afternoon will count twice and the capability profile will lie; decide one owner per moment and use the freed slots for what is missing, chiefly pretend play, oral vocabulary and a three-year-old saying 'stop' in words. I skipped only three lines: a duplicate, a program filed twice, and a private disclosure to a trusted adult that no observer can judge and that should not be a routine record. The could_not entries are honest as far as they go; knowledge and learning should have had one each, and technology's should have said that Grade 3, with no screen, cannot show five of its six preparatory behaviours. Finally, be plain with educators that a behaviour first seen at six is not late: the stage sets the ceiling, not the age at which a child should reach it.
